# Language and i18n rules (enforced by tools/guards: L1xx, L2xx)

- **English everywhere by default:** code comments, docstrings, commit messages, PR text,
  docs, ADRs, spike write-ups, agent files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/**`).
- **String literals are data** and may use any language (e.g. Unicode test fixtures), and so
  are data files under `tests/` (any file there that is not `.py`: `.sql`, `.json` fixtures).
- **Translations** are separate files next to the English source, named
  `<stem>-<LANG><suffix>` with an upper-case ISO 639-1 code: `README-KO.md`,
  `docs/design/design-KO.md`. Supported codes live in `docs/i18n.toml` (`languages`).
- The first line of a translation pins the English revision it was translated from *and* its
  own body: `<!-- i18n: source=README.md source-sha256=<12 hex> translation-sha256=<12 hex> -->`.
  Editing the English source reports the translation as stale (L202) right away - in the edit
  hook and pre-commit, not only in a full scan. Editing the translation without re-stamping is
  L204.
- Docs listed under `[required]` in `docs/i18n.toml` must ship every listed translation.
- **Changing an English source that has translations:** in the same change either update the
  translation and run `uv run python -m tools.guards i18n-stamp <translation>`, or hand it to
  the `translator` sub-agent. Never stamp a translation you did not actually update.
- The maintainer often writes in Korean. When a `-KO` translation was edited directly (L204):
  if the **meaning** changed, carry the change into the English source first, then re-stamp; if
  only the **wording** changed (style, natural phrasing), just re-stamp.
- Agent-facing files are never translated.
